title: Origins of the Cold War Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll see how WWII allies became Cold War enemies between 1945 and 1949.
meta_desc: GCSE History — Yalta, Potsdam, Truman, Marshall, Berlin Blockade and NATO.
final_note: You learned how Europe split between Truman Doctrine and Stalin's bloc.

concepts.def: WWII partnership of USA, USSR and Britain
February 1945 — agreed to split Germany and free elections
July 1945 — Truman replaced Roosevelt, tensions rose
1948 — $13 billion US aid to rebuild Europe
1948-49 — Western planes supplied blockaded West Berlin

walkthroughs.body_html:
At Yalta (Feb 1945) the Big Three agreed Germany would be split into four zones.

By Potsdam (July 1945) Roosevelt was dead and Truman had the atom bomb. Stalin refused free elections in Eastern Europe and the Grand Alliance cracked.

In March 1947 Truman pledged to support 'free peoples' resisting communism — the Truman Doctrine.

The Marshall Plan offered $13 billion in aid. Stalin refused it and set up Cominform (1947) and Comecon (1949) to control the East.

In June 1948 the Allies merged their zones and launched a new currency.

Stalin blockaded West Berlin. For 11 months the Berlin Airlift flew in 2 million tonnes of supplies. In April 1949 the West formed NATO — a military alliance against the USSR.
